subject: Pricing safety band & packaging options — redline review
messages:
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@novahealth.com>

Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>

Subject: Questions on pricing safety band and packaging in Order Form v3

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our procurement team reviewed OrderForm_v3 and had two substantive concerns before we can proceed to signatures: 1) the pricing "safety band" language (caps/floors) — specifically the minimum monthly spend floor; and 2) the packaging/ SKU bundling language in the pricing exhibit.

A couple of clarifying asks:
- Can you explain how the monthly floor interacts with the true-up at year-end? We want to avoid a hard charge that we can't reasonably predict.
- The exhibit lists a "bundle starter" price that seems higher than the per-unit list when combined with add-on modules. Are there discounts for multi-module bundles?

Attached is our redline of the order form (NH_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with comments in the pricing exhibit and an alternate clause request to remove the floor. Our legal counsel (cc'd) will review.

Best,
Sarah Johnson
VP, Vendor Management
NovaHealth

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick review and the redline. Short answers up front: the floor is intended as a minimum commitment to secure capacity & the discounted bundle pricing; the true-up is designed to credit against any shortfall rather than create an additional surprise charge. That said, we can make the mechanics clearer.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Pricing + Legal to propose alternate wording that ties the floor credit to future invoice credits or service credits (rather than a single immediate invoice).
- We'll add explicit bundle tiers in the pricing exhibit (e.g., Core + Embeddings + Support = bundled rate) and show the math.

I'm copying Lauren (pricing lead) and Marissa (contracts) to suggest language. If you're open, we can aim to resolve this today and circulate a clean order form for countersign.

Regards,

olga@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing safety band and packaging in Order Form v3

Sarah / team —

Thanks for the redline, Sarah. A few concrete concessions we can offer to make the floor less painful while preserving our economic protections:
1) Convert the "monthly floor" into a 12-month committed minimum (annualized) with quarterly true-ups. Any shortfall in the commitment will be reconciled as a credit applied to the next billing period over up to three quarters, rather than an immediate one-time invoice.
2) Add a grace band: for the first contract year, if usage is within 80-95% of the committed threshold, we apply a 50% mitigation on the shortfall credit.
3) For packaging, offer an explicit bundle discount schedule: 10% off list for Core+Embeddings, 18% off for Core+Embeddings+Support, and 25% for a full enterprise suite at >1M tokens/month. We'll include worked examples in the pricing_exhibit_v2.xlsx.

If those sound acceptable, Marissa can draft the exact clause. Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@novahealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>, Thomas Reed <t.reed@blawllp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing safety band and packaging in Order Form v3

Lauren / Olga —

Thanks — those are helpful movement items. A couple follow-ups from legal / procurement:
- The annualized 12-month committed minimum is acceptable, but the reconciliation window of three quarters is long; can we reduce to two quarters? Our finance team needs predictability for budget forecasting.
- For the grace band, can the mitigation be expressed as a fixed credit formula rather than a percentage (e.g., $X per 100k tokens below commited)? Easier for us to map to forecast models.
- For bundles: please include a line that clarifies that bundle discounts do not stack with other promotional or volume discounts (we need clear precedence).

Thomas from BLaw is cc'd — he may propose edits to the reconciliation and precedence language.

Best,
Sarah

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@novahealth.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing safety band and packaging in Order Form v3

Sarah / Thomas —

Drafting notes from legal:
1) Reconciliation window: we can agree to two quarters (6 months) provided the annual commitment remains firm and NovaHealth pays invoices as issued; that gives Redwood the cost visibility we need.
2) Grace band credit: we'll replace the % language with a fixed-credit table in the pricing exhibit (example: shortfall between 80%-95% = $3k credit per 100k tokens short; shortfall 60%-80% = $7k per 100k tokens). We'll include the exact table in the revised pricing_exhibit_v2.xlsx and annotate calculations.
3) Discount precedence: add a single precedence line: "Bundle discounts are primary; promotional discounts are applied only if expressly stated in writing and do not compound with bundle discounts."

I attached a redline of the clause language; please review and confirm. If accepted, we will reissue a clean Order Form with these exhibit tables for countersignature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Please confirm that credits will appear as line-item invoice adjustments.

If Redwood can confirm the invoice-credit mechanics and circulate the final clean Order Form, we'll route for signature on our end the same day.
